summary: Event density is high but concentrated in two places: a Democratic sweep of Congress overnight (futures up, dollar and yields down, gold back above $4,000, BTC sentiment hit but price +2%), and a cluster of 11-05 prints led by the held CARG (after the close tomorrow, one trading day out). CVS reported this morning (beat, raised guide, plan to split into two companies by H1 2028) and SMG reported (loss narrower than expected, FY27 guide in line), which closes both as open L2 items; no 4.01, 4.02 or new 5.02 filings in the 7-day window for any name. L2 applied: every symbol in the file was checked against its own estimate, 8-K 2.02 and 10-Q; GPOR and BJRI remain unverified.

event_risk.why: Held. Company-confirmed Q3 results 11-05 after the close (per earlier runs; the file estimate also says 11-05), 1 trading day out, so the reaction lands on 11-06. The thesis invalidates on a negative surprise inside five trading days, so the clause is live (L5). No filings or headlines in the window.

Held. Binance hack (about $6.3B, 10-29) is still unwinding: Binance now says about $2.85B was frozen or intercepted and that attackers got in through a fake job interview and an internal wallet-signing service. That is a security breach at one exchange with part of the loss recovered, and the exchange has not failed; the 'exchange failure' invalidation clause looks untripped on today's evidence, but the PM should state that (L5). Also: Santiment says a move above $79k could flip sentiment after the sweep-driven fear spike, BTC is up about 2% today, bears cite sub-$80k as unreclaimed (second day of 'needs to reclaim $80k'), Strategy spent $2.25B on buybacks with only about $133M of buyback cash left (STRC support question), and the MSCI decision on crypto-treasury index exclusion lands 11-11. Regulators approved equity perpetual futures on 11-03 (crypto equities +10-16%). Continues the 10-26 to 11-03 BTC flags; those graded mostly wrong at 5 days (price moves were small), so size this as a risk-watch item, not a signal.

Earnings 11-05 (company-announced per earlier runs), 1 trading day out. Evercore cut its PT to $145 from $160 on 11-03 (Outperform kept), the fifth PT cut in about a week after UBS, Jefferies, Baird and Wells Fargo. The drift flag from 11-02 is unresolved and now leans toward 'sell-side expects a soft print'.

Two threads collide. The AI-capex selloff (Apple memory-cost margin warning, Elliott hedging for a bear market, Howard Marks on AI valuations) is now joined by a political read: Dan Ives says 10% of planned US data centers 'will not happen now' after the Democratic sweep, and Evercore's 'nightmare' case (disputed sweep plus deeper Iran involvement) puts the S&P 500 down 10% by year-end. Against that, futures rose on the sweep, Tom Lee calls a bottom, and JPMorgan sees the S&P holding in all four midterm scenarios. Continues the 10-23 to 11-03 QQQ flags (graded wrong at 5 days, as the index fell further than flagged), so the direction of the flag has been right while its grading has been poor; it is a standing backdrop, not a new event.
Same backdrop as QQQ with a wider cushion; Evercore's downside case names VOO. Monthly jobs report (October NFP) later this week per earlier runs; it is not in today's input.

Gold back above $4,000 and gold and silver added about $1 trillion after the sweep on a weaker dollar and lower yields. That reverses the 10-31 support break and ETF outflows flagged on 11-03, but it is a one-day policy-driven move and Elliott and McGlone still call gold overextended. The 11-24 'earnings' date is a data artifact.

Yields fell with the dollar after the sweep. A Benzinga piece notes the record $1.36 trillion interest bill (fiscal 2026) rises under any midterm result, so gridlock gives only a limited calm. Earlier hawkish hold, 10-year near 5%, PCE 3.6% and December hike odds still stand; no rate decision in the window.

Deal event, not earnings: DoorDash buying Instacart at $65 (about $17B; 8-K 1.01 filed 10-29). Law firms are investigating the price (11-02). The file's 11-09 estimate (5 trading days) is moot. Merger-arb with FTC and political exposure, which a Democratic Congress does not reduce.

An 8-K 1.01/7.01/9.01 was filed 11-03; item numbers alone do not say what it is, and the $1.2B senior notes due 2037 priced 11-03 (refinancing) are the likeliest match, but that is an inference and the filing is unread. Separately, a data-inferred report says two of six Sabine Pass liquefaction trains may be offline (unconfirmed). TD Cowen raised its PT to $352 and Scotiabank to $327. Earnings passed 10-29.

Event passed: reported 11-02 (8-K 2.02, 10-K filed 11-03). Fell about 4% on 11-03 on memory-cost margin warnings. DZ Bank cut to Sell (PT $300) today and Barclays and KeyBanc sit at Underweight; the December-quarter sales guide of 7-10% growth stands. A Spanish CNMC sanction proceeding against Apple and Amazon is a small item. Next estimate 2027-01-28.

Adj EPS $2.09 vs $1.65, sales $108.4B vs $104.7B, FY26 adj EPS guide raised to at least $8.20 from $7.90-$8.10, operating cash flow guide to at least $15.5B, medical benefit ratio 91.3% vs 92.8%. 2027 targets: adj EPS at least $8.65, Health Services operating income at least $7B. Plan to split into an insurance/PBM company (Aetna, Caremark, Oak Street, Signify) and a retail pharmacy company by H1 2028. A $193M Omnicare guarantee charge is in the quarter and the Omnicare asset sale is called probable in Q4. Prior notes said the file's post-report estimate was unverified; the print was in fact today, so the file's 2027-02-09 date had jumped ahead of the report.

Company calls adjusted EPS above guidance. The 10-16 8-K 5.02 was never read and has aged out, so management-change risk stays unverified.

notable.headline: CVS Health Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Raises Full-Year Guidance; Announces Plan to Separate into Two Independent Companies
notable.read: A clean beat (adj EPS $2.09 vs $1.65), a raised FY26 guide to at least $8.20, 2027 targets of at least $8.65 EPS and at least $7B Health Services operating income, and a break-up (insurance/PBM versus retail pharmacy) targeted for H1 2028. Medical benefit ratio improved to 91.3% from 92.8%. The pre-open WSJ/FT leak on 11-03 was right. The separation is a multi-year execution story with a $193M Omnicare charge and a pending asset sale; Labor Department PBM disclosure rules remain a standing negative for Caremark.

notable.headline: Binance says about $2.85B frozen or intercepted; hackers used a bogus job interview and an internal wallet-signing service
notable.read: Cuts the net loss of the record hack (about $6.3B gross) and shows the breach was social engineering plus an internal signing service, not a protocol failure. For the held BTC position's 'exchange failure' clause this reads as a contained incident at one exchange; the PM should say so explicitly. Net flow remains negative (ETF outflows, $1.5B of liquidations after the hack, weak spot demand).

notable.headline: Bitcoin Fear Spikes on Democrat Sweep but $79,000 Could Flip the Script; Bitcoin Rallies 2%
notable.read: Sentiment fell on the sweep while price rose about 2% on supply-squeeze talk and shark-wallet accumulation. Santiment puts $79k as the level where fear turns contrarian; others still need an $80k reclaim. Crypto equities led on the 11-03 approval of equity perpetual futures. This is positioning noise, not a new risk driver.

notable.headline: Dan Ives: Democratic Sweep Will Slow AI Buildout, 10% Of Planned US Data Centers 'Will Not Happen Now'
notable.read: Turns the AI-capex worry from a valuation question into a policy-supply question and rests on one analyst's estimate. Offsets: futures up on the sweep, the AMD/Arista AI-spend datapoints, and Microsoft's 48% Azure growth on 11-03. Treat as sentiment with no filing behind it.

notable.headline: Evercore: midterm nightmare (disputed Democratic sweep plus deeper Iran involvement) puts the S&P 500 down 10% by year-end
notable.read: A stated tail scenario with a 6,800 S&P target, not a base case; the same analyst note set sits alongside JPMorgan's view that the S&P holds in all four outcomes. Fear & Greed was 19 (Extreme Fear) at the close on 11-03.

notable.headline: Gold, Silver Add $1 Trillion After US Midterm Results; Democratic Sweep Drops Dollar, Pushing Gold Past $4,000
notable.read: Reverses the 10-31 support break that was flagged on 11-03. Driven by a weaker dollar and lower yields after the sweep; whether it holds depends on this week's jobs data.

notable.headline: DZ Bank Downgrades Apple to Sell (PT $300); Apple Issues December-Quarter Revenue Guidance and Warns of Margin Pressures
notable.read: Continues the post-print margin story from 11-02 and 11-03: memory costs 'unprecedented', Siri AI expense, and a 45-46% gross margin guide, with PT cuts from JPMorgan ($355), Morgan Stanley ($350) and TD Cowen ($390) against raises from UBS, Baird and Argus. The dispersion is wide (Sell $300 to Buy $400); the downgrade adds a Sell, not a broad reversal.

notable.headline: Scotts Miracle-Gro Reports Fiscal 2026 Full-Year Results; sees FY2027 adj EPS $4.70-$4.90
notable.read: Print passed without a surprise: Q4 loss narrower than expected, sales a small miss, FY27 EPS guide in line with $4.71. Wells Fargo had raised its PT to $71 on 11-02 ahead of it. Dividend of $0.66 declared 11-03.

notable.headline: Evercore ISI Maintains Tapestry at Outperform, Lowers Price Target to $145 from $160
notable.read: Fifth sell-side PT cut in about a week ahead of the 11-05 print with ratings held, which usually signals expected estimate trimming rather than a thesis change. The 11-02 drift flag has not resolved and is still pointing the same way.

notable.headline: Citigroup Downgrades Adobe to Sell, PT $207
notable.read: A rating change to Sell on a software name with earnings 35 days out; not a held name. Adds to the broader pressure on software and AI beneficiaries seen in the QQQ coverage.

notable.headline: Morgan Stanley raises IDEXX PT to $810; Redburn to $700 from $665; UBS to $700
notable.read: Post-print PT raises continue after the 11-02 beat and guide raise. Supports the held thesis; it does not change the earlier point that the position has already moved sharply.

notable.headline: Chord Acquires Zenlytic, Adding Domino's To Enterprise Customer Portfolio
notable.read: Immaterial vendor news. What matters is the absence of confirmation for the 10-30 fiscal.ai guidance-cut item in four sessions: it looks like an echo of the 10-20 print and has so far come to nothing.

notable.headline: Law Firms Investigate Proposed Acquisition of Instacart by DoorDash
notable.read: Routine shareholder-rights solicitations around the $65 deal; extends the 11-02 and 11-03 notes. Not a deal break.

notable.headline: Operational disruption at Sabine Pass LNG facility / Cheniere Prices $1.2 Billion Senior Notes Offering
notable.read: The notes are a routine refinancing and probably match the 11-03 8-K 1.01. The Sabine Pass note is inferred from gas intake data and unconfirmed; if two of six trains are down it would be a real operating headwind. Analysts (TD Cowen $352, Scotiabank $327) still raised targets.

notable.headline: Walmart-Backed OnePay Enables Stablecoin Deposits
notable.read: Minor fintech item on a partner app; no change for the held position. The usual Walmart-tagged supplier product launches are noise.
